# How

On Codex, read the [platform mapping](../poteto-mode/references/codex-tools.md), including its per-skill notes, before following this skill.

On GitHub Copilot, read the [platform mapping](../poteto-mode/references/copilot-tools.md), including its per-skill notes, before following this skill.

Explore the codebase to answer "how does X work?" questions. Produce architectural explanations at the level of a senior engineer onboarding onto a subsystem, enough to build a working mental model, not so much that it reads like annotated source code.

Each spawn below names a role line in `pstack-models.md` and a default in [Models](#models). Set `model` to that line's value, or to the default if the sheet or the line is missing. Leave `model` unset when the value is `auto` or `inherit-parent`. If the `Agent` tool rejects a slug, use the default and say so. If it rejects the default, use the closest valid slug of the same family from its error message.

## Step 1. Assess Complexity

If the scope is ambiguous, state your interpretation and explore. The user can redirect.

- **Simple** (a single module, a small utility, a narrow question such as "how does function X work"): no explorers. One explainer explores and explains in a single pass. Go to Step 2b.
- **Complex** (a subsystem spanning multiple files or services, a cross-cutting feature, a full architectural overview): spawn parallel explorers first, then hand off to the explainer. Go to Step 2a.

When in doubt, take the simple path.

## Step 2a. Explore (complex questions only)

Decompose the question into 2 to 4 exploration angles, each a distinct slice of the subsystem. Spawn all explorers in a single message:

- `subagent_type`: `general-purpose`
- `model`: the `how explorer` line, default in [Models](#models)
- `readonly`: `true`

Each explorer gets the prompt in `references/explorer-prompt.md` with its angle filled in. Then go to Step 3.

## Step 2b. Direct Explain (simple questions)

Spawn one `Agent` subagent that explores and explains in one pass:

- `subagent_type`: `general-purpose`
- `model`: the `how explainer` line, default in [Models](#models)
- `readonly`: `true`

Build its prompt from `references/explainer-prompt.md` without the explorer-findings section. Go to Step 4.

## Step 3. Synthesize (complex questions only)

Once all explorers have returned, spawn one `Agent` subagent to synthesize their findings into one explanation:

- `subagent_type`: `general-purpose`
- `model`: the `how explainer` line, default in [Models](#models)
- `readonly`: `true`

Build its prompt from `references/explainer-prompt.md` with every explorer's findings filled in.

## Step 4. Present

Present the explainer's output to the user. Light edits for clarity or context from the conversation are fine. Do not substantially rewrite it.

## Output Format

The explanation uses the sections defined in `references/explainer-prompt.md`, dropping any that do not apply: Overview, Key Concepts, How It Works, Where Things Live, Gotchas.

## Models

Role defaults, stamped from `plugins/pstack/models.json` (edit there, rerun `tools/generate.mjs`). A matching role line in the `pstack-models.md` override sheet overrides each at runtime; `/setup-pstack` writes it and lists its path per runtime.

- how explorer: `opus`
- how explainer: `opus`

## Reasoning effort

A role value in the override sheet may name a reasoning effort after its model, as in `opus @xhigh`. Levels on Claude Code: `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, `max`. Which ones apply depends on the model. A value without `@` takes the sheet's `default effort` line, a level or `session`, and `session` when the sheet has no such line. `session` sets no effort, so the dispatch is the usual one. Strip the suffix before reading the model: `inherit-parent` or `auto` still omits `model` at every level, and a model name is passed as `model`. On Claude Code, a level picks the effort agent from the `subagent_type` you would otherwise use. `pstack:poteto-agent` becomes `subagent_type: "pstack:poteto-agent-<level>"`. `general-purpose`, or no `subagent_type`, becomes `subagent_type: "pstack:effort-<level>"`. The effort agents set only `effort`, so the model you pass still decides the model. On Codex, pass the level as `spawn_agent`'s `reasoning_effort` and keep the usual instructions.

content.text:
Aliasing coverage is **partial**. Extraction and identity resolution have good assertions; alias-based search and propagation into searchable database aliases have the biggest gaps. There’s no measured line or branch coverage available.

Existing tests cover:

- [Alias extraction](/Users/jamie/development/exposed/exposed/src/lib/domain/models/funder_name/tests.rs:52): `trading as`, `t/a`, normalization, primary-name preservation, and rejection of descriptive text as aliases.
- [Cleaning output](/Users/jamie/development/exposed/exposed/tests/declaration_cleaning.rs:314): extracted aliases survive cleaning.
- [Identity resolution](/Users/jamie/development/exposed/exposed/src/lib/domain/models/declaration_resolution/tests.rs:170): a legal name joins its alias despite a low score and missing addresses. The [Python worker test](/Users/jamie/development/exposed/resolution/tests/test_worker.py:53) checks alias-based candidate generation.
- [Database refresh](/Users/jamie/development/exposed/exposed/src/lib/outbound/declaration_loading/tests.rs:277): alias replacement, canonical-name inclusion, stable identity, orphan cleanup, retries, and rollback.
- [The real clean-and-resolve CLI test](/Users/jamie/development/exposed/exposed/tests/declaration_resolution_cli.rs:230): trading and legal names resolve together, but this test is ignored by default.

The highest-value missing test is **an alias-only search returning the canonical funder once**, with the expected score, threshold, and ranking. The [three funder search tests](/Users/jamie/development/exposed/exposed/src/lib/outbound/funder.rs:97) never populate aliases.

There’s also a propagation gap: the [loader builds persisted aliases from observed raw names](/Users/jamie/development/exposed/exposed/src/lib/outbound/declaration_loading.rs:421). No test proves that a brand mentioned only inside `trading as` becomes searchable after loading.

Other gaps include alias-to-alias matching, multiple or repeated aliases, and alias-specific company-number or entity-kind conflicts.

I ran all **six Python resolver tests successfully**. The focused Rust test could not compile offline because SQLx query-cache entries are missing, so Rust test outcomes remain unverified.

content.text:
Search compares your query with the canonical name and every stored alias, then uses the highest score. It returns the funder once, displaying its canonical name and ID. That’s how the [current query works](/Users/jamie/development/exposed/exposed/src/lib/outbound/funder.rs:22).

Use this synthetic test fixture:

| Canonical funder name | Stored aliases |
|---|---|
| Northstar Consulting Limited | Fletchers; Fletchers Group |

Search through the frontend:

```text
/api/search?term=Fletchers&max_entries=10&strictness=1
```

Expected behavior:

- `Northstar Consulting Limited` appears exactly once.
- Searching `Northstar Consulting Limited` returns the same funder ID.
- Removing its aliases from the test fixture makes the `Fletchers` search stop returning it.
- Restoring the aliases makes it appear again.

The backend’s direct endpoint is `/search` with the same parameters. The API doesn’t expose the score or matched alias.

This record would need to be created first. Keep the canonical name free of `Fletchers`: a name like `Northstar trading as Fletchers` can match through the canonical-name search alone, so it wouldn’t prove that alias lookup works.

I’m using pstack:architect to compare the type and query options. One caveat: the current `word_similarity(...) >= threshold` filter won’t use a GiST index by itself. PostgreSQL supports indexed word-distance ordering, which I’m checking as an option. [PostgreSQL documentation](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/pgtrgm.html).

+# Accepted design
+
+Use Astra's search-specific FunderSearchMatch wrapping canonical Funder and SearchMatchSource. Entity::Funder carries FunderSearchMatch; Entity::ParliamentMember stays unchanged. FunderRepo returns Vec<(FunderSearchMatch, SearchSimilarity)>; ParliamentMemberRepo and EntitySearchService retain their existing return structures. Remove obsolete From<&Funder> search conversion and migrate all callers. SearchMatchSource derives Serialize as an internally tagged enum: Name or Alias { name: String }. HTTP adds required `match_source`, name source for MPs. Frontend MP source type only permits Name, funder source permits both. Existing unknown-JSON parser checks the closed shape at its boundary, no missing-field fallback.
+
+Graft Sol's exact indexed query. Repository owns a read transaction, sets pg_trgm.word_similarity_threshold locally via sqlx macro to request strictness, then uses `funder_name %> query UNION SELECT funder_id WHERE funder_alias %> query` for candidate IDs. Indexed columns use exposed.gist_trgm_ops. Join candidates to canonical funder and lateral best alias scored with word_similarity(query,alias), score desc then alias COLLATE C asc, LIMIT1 per funder. Compute best exact score with GREATEST and alias source only if alias score > canonical score. Keep inclusive exact score >= threshold authoritative, deterministic identity ordering after score, SQL identity LIMIT after dedup. Member query uses corresponding indexable name operator and exact score threshold/order/SQL LIMIT in repository-owned local-setting transaction. Keep scores from word_similarity rather than rounded distance. Preserve current merge's equal-score MP/funder pair interleaving. PostgreSQL18 observation confirms predicate includes scores at0,1; add interior equality regression and pooled-setting reset check. Keep all queries sqlx macros.
+
+Add three GiST indexes on members.name, funders.funder_name and funder_aliases.funder_alias to reversible baseline; table down drops suffice but make reversibility clear. Add repeatable non-destructive db/upgrades/search_trigram_indexes.sql and concise db/README.md guidance for existing database preservation/schema verification/SHA384 synchronization. Do not add a migration version or mutate live schema in delegate. Live DB upgrade is parent-owned after tests.
+
+UI uses current layout/type/color. Canonical name remains main linked label. Alias source gets visible secondary `Matched alias: {original alias}` within the text column, with plaintext highlighting and accessible association to link. Direct name source no extra label. Narrow layouts wrap long alias without pushing kind/icon columns offscreen. Help text can mention names and aliases if useful.
+
+Meaningful verification: DB alias-only result, best alias original spelling, direct winner/tie, alias ties, one identity with many aliases doesn't consume limit, strictness0/1/interior exact boundary, ranking and pooled threshold reset; service/HTTP metadata retention; browser alias explanation, direct source no label, canonical navigation, hostile alias escaping, narrow layout, malformed metadata rejection. Full relevant Rust suite and frontend check/build/browser tests; real local API/UI driven with isolated fixtures plus snapshots. Check GiST index definitions and access plan without performance claims.
